nodes.label: Divergent ai-chatbot window creation sites
nodes.summary: The AI Companion popup is built from two unrelated places, a cold-create in trigger/ai_handler.rs and showAiChatbotPopup in apps/web/src/utils/companion.ts, and they disagreed on resizable, background_color, title and position.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - f1-unify-ai-chatbot-window-options [ses_f0653e333ffe4kbmjlkqIg9QmB].md:L00038] Because `app.get_webview_window("ai-chatbot")` (Rust) and `WebviewWindow.getByLabel("ai-chatbot")` (TS) read the SAME label registry, whichever side creates first permanently fixes the options for that window's lifetime.

nodes.label: Both ai-chatbot creators resolve against one label registry, so the first writer fixes the options for that window's lifetime
nodes.norm_label: both ai-chatbot creators resolve against one label registry so the first writer fixes the options for that window's lifetime
nodes.summary: Mechanism recorded in the module doc of the new companion_window.rs: both creators look the window up by the same label, so whichever runs first wins and its options are then immutable for the life of that window.

nodes.label: One documented Rust declaration plus a TS mirror, kept in step by a source guard running in both directions
nodes.norm_label: one documented rust declaration plus a ts mirror kept in step by a source guard running in both directions
nodes.summary: The fix adopted for the divergent ai-chatbot options: a Rust const in companion_window.rs plus a TS mirror in companion.ts, with include_str! source guards that parse the other language's source and compare every shared field in each direction.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - f1-unify-ai-chatbot-window-options [ses_f0653e333ffe4kbmjlkqIg9QmB].md:L7848] No side can read the other's declarations at runtime, so this is one documented Rust declaration plus a TS mirror, with a source guard running in **both** directions; a shared JSON was rejected because it is outside the write scope, it would **weaken** TS type-checking (`backgroundColor` widens to `number[]`, needing a cast away from `Color`), and the brief said not to invent a new cross-file mechanism.

nodes.label: Rust owns the ai-chatbot title localization; the TS side must not re-localize it
nodes.norm_label: rust owns the ai-chatbot title localization the ts side must not re-localize it
nodes.summary: Resolution of the title divergence: the localized title comes from Rust's locale table via NativeKey::WindowAiCompanion, and the TS mirror carries only the locale table's English row as title_fallback. The divergence is narrowed but not eliminated, since eliminating it needs out-of-scope IPC.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - f1-unify-ai-chatbot-window-options [ses_f0653e333ffe4kbmjlkqIg9QmB].md:L07791] Justification, in order: (1) the frontend has no i18n key for this string and there is no `#[tauri::command]` in `locale.rs` and no `get_native_text` anywhere, so the webview *cannot* produce the localized title without new IPC — which is outside this chunk's write scope; (2) the window is `decorations:false` + `skip_taskbar:true`, so the title renders nowhere, meaning the TS literal can only ever drift, and it had; (3) the alternative I considered and rejected — omitting `title` so Rust "owns" it — is worse: Tauri's JS create path goes `from_config` → `with_config`, which has no locale fallback, so the window would get an **empty** title.

nodes.label: resizable: true buys window-manager drag-resize, not the JS resize grip
nodes.norm_label: resizable true buys window manager drag resize not the js resize grip
nodes.summary: Measured correction of the brief's stated rationale: AiChatbotResizeHandle calls win.setSize(), which Tauri does not gate on resizable, and isResizable has zero hits repo-wide, so nothing reads the flag. The flag must still be true, but because the window shows a resize handle and true restores the WM frame-edge resize that existed only when the Rust path won the race.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - f1-unify-ai-chatbot-window-options [ses_f0653e333ffe4kbmjlkqIg9QmB].md:L07789] The grip in `AiChatbotResizeHandle.tsx` calls `win.setSize()`, and Tauri does **not** gate that on `resizable` — confirmed, `isResizable` has **zero** hits repo-wide, so nothing reads the flag.

nodes.label: A plan status verdict needs verifiable evidence, not ticked checkboxes
nodes.norm_label: a plan status verdict needs verifiable evidence not ticked checkboxes
nodes.summary: The verdict discipline of this audit: plan prose and progress/evidence files are treated as claims, not evidence, every acceptance criterion gets checked against files, tests and code paths, and a criterion whose only proof is a green run is marked UNVERIFIED.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-26 - assess-3-plans-website-i18n-speech [ses_f208d0ac2ffeQ2fupDNrEF3u2W].md:L57] Mixed or absent evidence means INCONCLUSIVE. A wrong "FINISHED" is far worse than an honest "INCONCLUSIVE", because the plan's status will be changed on the strength of your answer.
